findings: §5.2 'commit early' rule says to substitute 'the shortest block remaining in your rail' if your block is exposed before all cups land, but gives no ruling for the case (explicitly acknowledged elsewhere in §8, 'a player has exactly one block left') where the exposed block is your ONLY block — there is nothing left to substitute.

§5.2 lets any player force a full re-commit ('every player lifts their cup, returns their block to the rail, and the count is run again') if they think the Commit wasn't simultaneous, with no cap on how many times this can be invoked per round — an unlimited stalling/re-read vector, notable since the setter alone holds private information about the gap.

§8 covers 'everyone's rail is empty, or only one player can still commit' by saying 'play the round anyway with whoever can commit,' but never rules on the case where LITERALLY NO ONE can commit (all rails empty, some lines still nonempty, game not yet at Bottom) — the Commit step (§5.2) is stated as mandatory for 'every player with at least one block,' so it's unclear whether the round is simply skipped straight to the next Set or something else happens.

§6's claim that Bottom is reached 'within 16 rounds' (worst case, all setters choosing the 2-click net drop) treats only the net drop as consuming the 31-click budget, but §5.1's Set mechanic overshoots downward first (5/6/7 gross clicks) before correcting up by 3/2/1 — so the screw's actual lowest point during a Set can hit the bottom stop earlier than the net-sum arithmetic implies. The rulebook doesn't reconcile this, so the stated round-count ceiling is questionable.

§8's false-'Bottom'-call ruling ('if it turns, the call was false... the game continues from the bar's actual position') doesn't say whether the verifying player's downward turn(s) during the check are kept (permanently lowering the bar outside of a proper Set) or must be wound back up before play resumes.
